function: Joint hybrid precoding (digital plus phase-modulation-array analog) at the access points and RIS phase-shift design, learned by a CNN to maximize sum rate (p. 8).
system: Cell-free mmWave MIMO: M=2 APs with 16 antennas and 4 RF chains, K=4 single-antenna users, R=8 passive reflecting RISs of 64 elements; carrier frequency not stated (p. 9).
method: Unsupervised CNN (3 conv layers, 2 fully connected layers, constraint layer) trained offline with a negative sum-rate loss and Adam; no labels (pp. 8-9).
data_channel: Own simulated Saleh-Valenzuela ULA mmWave channels (AP-RIS one LoS path, RIS-user 20 paths, uniform angles, path loss exponent 2.2); 640,000 random channels, 8:2 train/validation split (pp. 5, 9).
test_conditions: Trained on 640,000 random channels (p. 9); results sweep transmit power, number of RISs and antennas; no unseen scenario or fine-tuning stated (pp. 11-12).
baselines: Non-learned only: FP-based [23], ZF-based [19] joint precoding and RIS design, LS-based hybrid precoding [35], WMMSE [30], the proposed iterative design, random RIS; no learned baseline (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Sum rate, energy efficiency, convergence in iterations, and training and validation loss (pp. 10-12).
complexity: CNN: O(K NU R NR + M NA R NR) (p. 9); iterative design: O(Niter(M(NA^3+NRF^3) + M K NRF^3 + R^3 NR^3)) (p. 7).
q1_support: p. 5: "the Saleh-Valenzuela channel model with uniform linear array (ULA) is employed". Custom simulator with uniform random angles (p. 9); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 9: "the ratio of training set to verification set is 8:2", a held-out part of the same data. No test of the trained CNN on another scenario, band or configuration is stated; Figs. 12, 15, 16 (pp. 11-12) vary RISs and antennas without saying the model is reused or adapted.
q3_support: p. 10: "the ZF-based and FP-based joint FDP and RIS design algorithms [19], [23] are taken as benchmarks". All benchmarks are non-learned (ZF, FP, LS, WMMSE, random RIS); no earlier learned method or standard network is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "formulated as O (KNU RNR + M NA RNR )" for the CNN; the iterative design also has an order (p. 7).
q5_support: p. 9: "640,000 random combined channels are taken as training data", generated by the authors' own simulator. No code or data link and no public dataset appear in the text.
notes: Included, area 3: the unsupervised CNN outputs the AP hybrid precoders and the RIS phase shifts (p. 8), and the main metric is sum rate. The iterative WMMSE/BCD design (pp. 6-7) is a non-learned companion method of the paper. q2 is graded 0 under the explicit rule: the CNN input and output sizes depend on the number of RISs and antennas (p. 8), yet Figs. 12, 15 and 16 show the CNN curve for other numbers of RISs and antennas and the paper does not say whether it was retrained or reused, so the reviewer may want to check those figures. The legends of Figs. 8, 9, 11-16 (pp. 10-12) list no learned baseline.
